item.title: DataLab Office Hours (in person) — Tue Oct 27, 1:00 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
DataLab offers free in person drop-in office hours during which UC Davis researchers can obtain data science help and advice on working with their data. During these short, just-in-time sessions we meet with faculty, students, postdoctoral scholars, and staff from all domains across the University. Depending on the nature of your question and our availability, it may be possible to schedule a longer follow-up consultation after your office hours visit.
Appointments are not required. Please complete the brief office hours intake form ahead of time to help us connect you with the right expert for your question.
Common office hours help topics include:
Open Source Programming (R, Python, Julia, etc.)Reproducible research computing and data scienceResponsible and ethical data scienceData gathering, organization, databases, and experimental designData analysis, statistics, and explorationData visualizationMachine learning and neural networksText mining and natural language processingGeos

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Oct 28, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Halloween in the UC Davis Bee Haven Garden — Wed Oct 28, 3:00 PM — UC Davis Bee Haven
item.description: Wednesday, October 28 | 3:00-5:00 PM | 1 Bee Biology Rd., Davis | Free The pollinators are getting into the Halloween spirit, and you’re invited to join them! Come to the UC Davis Bee Haven, a pollinator garden full of bees, butterflies, and the flowers they love, for a spooky pollination adventure. It’ll be fun for kids, teens, UC Davis students, and every bee, butterfly, and plant fan in between. Wander through the garden and meet the pollinators and plants that call our local haven home. Along the way, you’ll collect nectar and pollen, then trade them in for sweet candy and sticker rewards. There are also hands-on crafts and activities for all ages, so everyone can join in at their own pace. Costumes are required, so wear whatever you like, whether it’s spooky, silly, handmade, or pollinator-inspired. Bring the whole family, your friends, or your lab mates for a free afternoon of Halloween fun. Parking: Parking is available right in front of the garden and in front of the Harry

item.title: Savor: Fresh Starts — How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat — Wed Oct 28, 5:00 PM — Peter J. Shields Library
item.description: The formation of the Davis Farmers Market 50 years ago was a revolutionary movement to connect consumers directly to farmers and helped shape the fresh flavors of California cuisine. Markets have been a cornerstone of the community and have also played a pivotal role in food access, especially during supply chain shortages and widespread food recalls. Inevitably, markets have evolved. Join us as we explore the history, impact and changing role of farmers markets in local communities. The event will feature a panel of leading industry experts including: – Ann Evans, UC Davis alumna, co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and Davis Food Co-op, author and former mayor and city council member of the City of Davis – Sam Greenlee, chief executive officer of Alchemist Community Development Corporation – Chutharat Sae Tong, co-owner of Majka Pizzeria and Bakery in Sacramento – Moderator Catherine Brinkley, associate professor in Human Ecology, Community and Regional Development at UC Davis A

item.title: Figure Drawing Group — Wed Oct 28, 6:30 PM — Pence Gallery
item.description: Figure Drawing Group Wednesday, October 28, 6:30-9 PM $15 Members, $22 Non-Members | Limited to 10 participants Registration & payment is required in advance through the Pence’s website. We hold self-guided figure drawing sessions with a nude model every 2nd & 4th Wednesday of the month, from 6:30-9 PM. This group is for both experienced artists and amateurs to have an opportunity to draw from the nude model. If you have never drawn from a live model before and would like to join us, you are very welcome! People of all skill levels, ages 18 and up, are welcome and encouraged to join. This is not a class, and no instruction is provided. The atmosphere is relaxed and non-competitive. Bring your own art materials, and we’ll provide a comfortable place to sketch or paint live models in our upstairs classroom space. item.title: Volunteers Wanted - Trick-or-Treat — Thu Oct 29, 3:00 PM
item.description:
UC Davis Student Parent Family Trick-or-Treating is on Thursday, October 29th, from 3- 5 p.m. Children of student parents will be trick-or-treating their way through UC Davis while programs and centers hand out candy.
GSP is looking for 3 - 5 volunteers to hand out candy to little monsters, princesses, and ghosts on the porch of South Hall. Candy will be provided. All you need to do is hand out candy and make a little one happy!
You are encouraged (but not required) to dress up fully or partially (Halloween shirt, headband, face makeup, etc.). If you can volunteer for 1 hour or 2 hours, please indicate that in the questions below.
For questions, contact Valeri at vqgarcia@ucdavis.edu
Source: UC Davis CampusGroups

item.title: Principles of Community Celebration — Tue Nov 10, 4:00 PM — UC Davis ARC
item.description:
The 2026 Principles of Community Celebration recognizes the people and partnerships that bring our values to life across UC Davis. The celebration will feature recognition of the Soaring to New Heights and ASUCD awards honorees, stories from faculty, staff and students, showcases highlighting community-engaged research and partnerships, and opportunities to connect with colleagues and community partners.
We honor our collective decision to be part of this community, and we celebrate the ongoing work of making UC Davis a place people want to be. For more information, visit: https://excellence.ucdavis.edu/events/principles-community-celebration.

item.description:

Interdisciplinary artist Gioia Fonda has long collected colorful toys, both for their intrinsic charm and as creative inspiration. As a student at California College of the Arts, she arranged small collectibles into still-life compositions, captured them on film, and processed the photos at a local drugstore. Captivated by these arrangements, her advisor, Charlie Gill, painted spare compositions based on her photographs—works that now hang alongside hers. For this exhibition, Fonda has created a series of new paintings featuring similar arrangements of toys and found objects. She is also offering an opportunity for members of the public to exhibit their own small works on paper, riffing on some of her recent photos. Artists may add to this display throughout th

item.title: Bohème Bewitched — Wed Oct 28, 3:00 PM — Bohème Bewitched
item.description:

Six enchanted lands inside the old bank at 300 E Street, downtown Davis: the old Union Bank building at the corner of 3rd and E, next to Panera Bread, one block from Central Park. Hours: Wednesday to Friday 3:00 to 6:30pm. Saturday and Sunday 11:00am to 6:30pm. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays. Open 11am to 6:30pm on Saturday, October 31. $4 at the door for the experience, credited to any $8 purchase in the shop (same visit only). Open to all ages every day until 6:30pm. Enchanted Evenings: special evening events run 7 to 9:30pm on Oct 23, 24 and 30. $13 online, $15 at the door. Every date, hours and tickets: bohemebewitched.com

item.description:
Tim McNary Live @ The Melon Ball in Davis Tim McNary is a Cinematic Folk Artist from the Southern United States. He found his passion for songwriting while backpacking throughout South America after college. The Nashville based songwriter traverses emotional and geographical borders with multi-dimensional songwriting and evocative vocals. item.title: City of Davis Wetlands Tour — Sun Nov 1, 9:00 AM — 45400 County Road 28H
item.description:
The Davis Wetlands is a managed, native California wetland ecosystem that includes oak riparian woodlands and native grasslands. The group will caravan along the hard-packed gravel roads of the auto tour route. Several stops will be made along the way providing guests with a closer look at the many species of birds that utilize the more than 400 acres of reconstructed wetlands. Meet at the City of Davis Wastewater Treatment Plant. 45400 County Rd 28H, Davis, CA 95616. There is no access to restrooms in the City of Davis Wetlands; please arrange for this before arriving. Tours run rain or shine at 9:00 a.m. on the first Sunday of each month, except in the instances of flooding. Registration required.

item.title: Kensuke Yamada: Ceramic Sculptures Between Folklore and the Modern World — Wed Oct 28 — John Natsoulas Gallery
item.description: October 28–November 28, 2026 Opening Reception: October 30, 7–9 p.m. The John Natsoulas Gallery is pleased to present a solo exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Kensuke Yamada, an artist whose distinctive figurative works fuse Japanese cultural traditions, contemporary visual culture, and an enduring fascination with the human condition. Combining references to folklore, mythology, and popular imagery with exaggerated forms and richly worked surfaces, Yamada creates figures that are simultaneously humorous, unsettling, and emotionally resonant. In this new body of work, his characteristic playfulness takes on a greater sense of urgency, reflecting the pressures and uncertainties of contemporary life. Born in Kamakura, Japan, Yamada grew up surrounded by the country’s historic architecture, religious imagery, and long tradition of ceramic sculpture. item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Wed Oct 28, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Wed Oct 28, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt
